extracted.intended_audience: researchers (postdoctoral to senior) seeking information on ERC and Marie Skłodowska-Curie personal grants, especially TU/e researchers
extracted.subtask_short: applying for ERC and Marie Curie grants
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of eligibility, purpose, types, and basic rules for ERC personal grants (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced, Synergy) and Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowships (European and Global). Useful as an initial checklist for prospective applicants evaluating fit and mobility/duration constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC support for frontier/pioneering research
rubrics_metrics.description: European Research Council (ERC) grants support talented researchers of any nationality and age who wish to pursue their frontier research. The ERC encourages in particular pioneering ideas that address new and emerging fields and applications that introduce unconventional, innovative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ERC funding is aimed at high-risk/high-gain frontier research; applicants should propose pioneering ideas, new/emerging fields or unconventional approaches. ERC offers several personal grant types (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced) and the Synergy Grant for collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting Grants: eligibility (2–7 years post-PhD) and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 2-7 years of experience since the completion of their PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must fall within the 2–7 year post-PhD window and demonstrate early-career excellence via track record and proposal quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grants: eligibility (7–12 years post-PhD) and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 7-12 years of experience since completion of PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must fall within the 7–12 year post-PhD window and show a consolidating track record plus a strong proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grants: expectation of significant recent achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for active researchers with a track-record of significant research achievements in the last 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced Grant applicants are senior researchers; emphasis is on a substantial record of significant achievements within the last decade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergy Grant: collaborative PI opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC also offers an opportunity for collaboration between Principal Investigators in the Synergy Grant scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synergy Grants are aimed at groups of PIs working together on ambitious research that benefits from complementary expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marie Curie Postdoctoral Fellowships: purpose and target
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of Postdoctoral Fellowships (PFs) is to support researchers’ careers and foster excellence in research. The Postdoctoral Fellowships action targets researchers holding a PhD who wish to carry out their research activities abroad, acquire new skills and develop their careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PFs are mobility-focused: they help researchers gain experience in other countries, disciplines and non-academic sectors; intended for PhD holders seeking career development through international experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marie Curie European Fellowship: mobility, duration, and nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: They are open to researchers moving within Europe or coming to Europe from another part of the world to pursue their research career. These fellowships take place in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and can last between 1 and 2 years. Researchers of any nationality can apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: European Fellowships require the researcher to be hosted in an EU/Associated country; duration is 1–2 years; there is no nationality restriction for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marie Curie Global Fellowship: mobility, duration, and return phase requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: They fund the mobility of researchers outside Europe. The fellowship lasts between 2 to 3 years, of which the first 1 to 2 years will be spent in a non-associated Third Country, followed by a mandatory return phase of 1 year to an organisation based in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. Only nationals or long-term residents of the EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries can apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global Fellowships require outbound mobility (1–2 years) plus a compulsory 1-year reintegration to an EU/Associated host; eligibility is limited to EU/Associated country nationals or long-term residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal and track record expectations (general ERC requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Starting and Consolidator Grants the page specifies a 'scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Across ERC personal grants the quality of the research proposal and the applicant's track record are central eligibility/selection considerations—demonstrable promise for early-career schemes and significant achievement for Advanced Grants.
